about.features:
- Three analyses: single plot, multiple plots (spatial) and temporal (one plot over the years).
- Reads `.xlsx`, `.csv` and `.txt`, normalises column names and finds the table and the plot area.
- Species resolved from an editable regional species table (names, codes and genus abbreviations).
- Density, basal area, mean DBH, mean and canopy height, stems per tree and mortality.
- Relative density, dominance and frequency, and the importance value (IVI).
- DBH classes with configurable cutoffs and the Holdridge complexity index.
- A data-check panel, publication-quality figures and PDF, Excel and CSV exports.

about.method:
- Cintrón, G. & Schaeffer-Novelli, Y. (1984). Methods for studying mangrove structure. In: Snedaker, S.C. & Snedaker, J.G. (eds), *The mangrove ecosystem: research methods*. UNESCO, Paris, pp. 91-113.
- Holdridge, L.R. (1967). *Life zone ecology*. Tropical Science Center, San José.
- Pool, D.J., Snedaker, S.C. & Lugo, A.E. (1977). Structure of mangrove forests in Florida, Puerto Rico, Mexico, and Costa Rica. *Biotropica* 9(3): 195-212.
- Estrada, G.C.D. (2013). *Análise espaço-temporal do sequestro e estoque de carbono na biomassa aérea de manguezais*. PhD thesis, Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro.
- Soares, M.L.G. et al. (2017). Mangrove forests associated with salt flats: a case study from southeast Brazil. *Brazilian Journal of Oceanography* 65(2): 102-115.

about.what: MangueTREE is an open-source Python engine with a Streamlit interface for the structural and phytosociological analysis of mangrove forest plots. It reads field inventories (one row per stem), checks the data, and computes the parameters used in mangrove structure studies.

home.computes:
- **Structure:** density (stems/ha), basal area (m²/ha), mean DBH, mean and canopy height, stems per tree, mortality (stems and basal area).
- **Phytosociology:** relative density, dominance and frequency, and the **importance value (IVI)**; Cintrón & Schaeffer-Novelli (1984).
- **DBH classes:** distribution by diameter class (configurable cutoffs).
- **Holdridge complexity index**, computed for DBH > 2.5 cm and DBH > 10 cm; Pool, Snedaker & Lugo (1977).
- **Spatial comparison** between plots and **temporal analysis** of one plot over the years.
- **Export** of tables (Excel/CSV) and **PDF reports**.
home.description: MangueTREE turns field inventories of mangrove plots into structural and phytosociological parameters, DBH class distributions and comparisons between plots and over the years. Upload a spreadsheet, review the data-check panel and export the tables and figures.
home.examples: Two example files from the Guaratiba mangrove (Rio de Janeiro, Brazil) are in the `data/` folder of the [repository]({repo}): `guaratiba_T2_2009.xlsx` (three plots, one sheet per plot; for Single plot and Multiple plots) and `guaratiba_H2_2003_2025.xlsx` (plot H2 surveyed 15 times; for Temporal).

home.format_intro: The file has **one row per stem**. The columns below are recognised; the essential ones are `tree_id`, `species`, `dbh_cm` and `condition`. A tree with several stems repeats its `tree_id` in each row.
home.format_pt_headers: Portuguese field headers are also accepted, for example `Indivíduo`, `Nº tr's`, `Espécie`, `DAP`, `Alt. Corr.` and `Condição`.

map.no_coordinates: The file has no coordinate columns (latitude and longitude), so there is no map to show.
method.dbh_classes: Default DBH classes: below 2.5 cm, 2.5 to below 10 cm, and 10 cm or more; the cutoffs can be changed in the sidebar (Cintrón & Schaeffer-Novelli 1984, p. 92). A stem of exactly 2.5 cm falls in the middle class and one of exactly 10 cm in the upper class.
method.heights_live_only: Mean height, its standard deviation and canopy height use live stems only: the field protocol used at NEMA/UERJ does not record height on dead trees (Estrada 2013, p. 151).
method.holdridge: CI = s · d · b · h · 10⁻³, where s = number of species, d = number of stems, b = basal area (m²) and h = stand height (m), all per 0.1 ha; Holdridge (1967), as applied to mangroves by Pool et al. (1977). In each index, s, d and b use only live stems with DBH above the cutoff. Adaptation: h is the mean of the 10 tallest live-stem heights in the plot (Pool et al. 1977 used the tallest tree of each subplot).
method.ivi_multi: IVI = RDe + RDo + RF (relative density, dominance and frequency), with RF based on the % of plots in which the species occurs (Cintrón & Schaeffer-Novelli 1984, p. 96). Density and basal area pool the stems over the summed plot areas.
method.ivi_needs_units: The IVI needs more than one sampling unit, because frequency depends on them (Cintrón & Schaeffer-Novelli 1984, p. 96). For a single plot the table shows relative density and relative dominance. The IVI is on the Multiple plots page.
method.mean_dbh: Mean DBH is the diameter of the tree of mean basal area (the quadratic mean), not the arithmetic mean of the DBH values (Cintrón & Schaeffer-Novelli 1984).
method.q_note: The De Liocourt quotient q is descriptive; its interpretation depends on the stand context.
